_comment: Hand-maintained mapping from OpenAI's public pricing page to pricing.json entries.
No model list is held here: the page lists the models, under their API ids.
`source` is the page's Markdown, which OpenAI serves beside every docs page (the
page's address plus .md): every tab of the rendered page, as plain Markdown tables.
`sections` and `speeds` are the lines that head the page's parts: a table belongs to
the last section and the last speed above it. A speed is named in every form the page
has headed it: OpenAI headed the Flex tab `#### Flex` until 2026-11-18 and heads it
with a bare `Flex` line and a `### Flex pricing data` heading since, so both are
named, and a revert reads Flex rather than folding its tables into Batch, which are
the same prices. `tables_not_read` names a heading whose tables are deliberately not
read; every other `### <speed> pricing data` line the page serves is named in
`speeds`, or the run fails rather than reading its tables as the speed above it.
`tables` names every table read, by
its section, its speeds and its header row, word for word, and says what its
columns become. A table the page has and `tables` does not name is reported in the
run's notes and not read; one named in `required_tables` that the page lacks fails
the run. A Standard table gives a model's entry, a Batch table the `_batch` fields
of the same entry, a Flex, Fast or Ultrafast table an entry of its own,
`<id> (flex)`, `<id> (fast)`, `<id> (ultrafast)`.
`long_context_note` is the sentence that says where long context starts:
'Short context: ≤272K input tokens. Long context: >272K input tokens.' gives
long_context_threshold 272001, K read as 1,000.
Not published, and why (scripts/providers/openai/README.md says more): the models
whose category carries `restricted_marker` ('Trusted Access'), sold only to
organisations OpenAI approves; the sections in `sections_not_read`: fine-tuning,
closed to new users, and the cloud platforms, which bill through their own pages;
and the tables in `tables_not_read` below.
_comment_tables_not_read: Tables the page states and this site does not publish, by the line that heads them.
`### Ultrafast list pricing data` states what Ultrafast will cost from 2027-03-01: the
page's prose above it says 'For GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, Ultrafast costs 3 times
the Standard rate through February 28, 2027, and 6 times the Standard rate starting
March 1, 2027 (Pacific time)', so the table in force today is the promotion one, read
as Ultrafast. Published, the list prices would be today's prices, which they are not.
At the switch the promotion table leaves the page, the Ultrafast entries go
`absent_since`, and that is the signal to read the list table instead.
long_context_note: Short context: ≤(?P<short>[0-9]+)K input tokens\. Long context: >(?P<long>[0-9]+)K input tokens\.
_comment_tools: The tools table prices each row in a sentence. Each row read is named here by its
Tool and Details cells, with the pattern its price must match (`amount` is the
figure) and the field it becomes. A row not named here is reported and not read; a
row named here that the table lacks, or prices another way, fails the run.
Containers state one price per memory size, `variant`, each published as its own
entry, `containers (4 GB)`, priced per 20-minute session as the page states it.
